directAnswer: Pope John XII (reigned 955–964), born Octavian, was the son of Alberic II and became pope as a young man of about eighteen. He crowned Otto I as emperor in 962, a turning point in European history, but soon broke with him, was deposed by an imperial synod in 963, and died in 964 after briefly regaining Rome.

paras: Octavian was born into the family that had ruled Rome for half a century. His father, Alberic II, made the Roman nobility swear to elect him pope, and in December 955 he succeeded Agapetus II while also inheriting his father's civil authority. He was very young, and contemporaries, especially the hostile chronicler Liutprand of Cremona, portrayed him as unsuited to the office.

Liutprand's account, written for Otto's court, contains many accusations of personal misconduct. Historians accept that John's conduct gave serious grounds for criticism while recognizing that the most lurid details come from a partisan source.

sections.h2: The Coronation of Otto I in 962
paras: John's position grew dangerous when Berengar II, king of Italy, pressed on papal territory. The pope turned to Otto I of Germany for help. Otto came to Rome, and on 2 February 962 John crowned him and his wife Adelaide in St. Peter's. The event is often regarded as the beginning of what later became known as the Holy Roman Empire.

Days later Otto issued the document known as the Diploma Ottonianum, confirming the papacy's territorial possessions while asserting imperial rights, including a role in the oversight of papal elections. Around the same time John authorized the creation of an archdiocese at Magdeburg to organize missions among the Slavs.

The alliance did not last. Fearing Otto's dominance, John opened negotiations with Berengar's son Adalbert and with other powers. Otto returned to Rome in 963, and John fled. A synod convened under Otto's authority in November 963 heard accusations against the pope and, when he refused to appear, declared him deposed. The synod then elected a layman, who became Leo VIII.
The legitimacy of deposing a pope in this way was questionable even at the time, and the episode remains one of the most debated in papal history.

Once Otto left Rome, John returned in early 964. He held a synod that annulled the decisions against him and punished some of his opponents. He died on 14 May 964, outside Rome, while still in his twenties. Liutprand gives a scandalous account of his death, but the true circumstances are not known with certainty. Historians mark his death as the close of the so-called saeculum obscurum, the period of noble domination of the papacy.

keyFacts: Born Octavian, son of Alberic II; elected at about eighteen
Crowned Otto I emperor on 2 February 962
Deposed by a synod under Otto in 963; returned to Rome in 964

faqs.question: Why is John XII's coronation of Otto I important?
faqs.answer: It renewed the Western imperial title in Germany and is commonly seen as the start of the Holy Roman Empire, binding papal and imperial politics together for centuries.

faqs.question: Was John XII validly deposed?
faqs.answer: A synod summoned by Otto I declared him deposed in 963, but the procedure was irregular and contested. John reversed it after returning to Rome, and his status remains a matter of historical debate.

faqs.question: How reliable are the accusations against John XII?
faqs.answer: Many come from Liutprand of Cremona, a writer loyal to Otto I. Historians take his charges seriously but recognize his strong bias.
